## TL;DR

Remote runner failures now say what went wrong and what to do next. Test connection names each failing host with a plain-English cause and next step, and keeps the raw ssh or probe output under "Details". The probes run in parallel, so an unreachable host costs one 15-second wait, not one per host. Removing a host from the pool asks for confirmation first. Everything is covered by fixture tests and by a headless WebKit pass at 375, 768 and 1280 px.

One thing needs a human decision. The scoped `repoos check` runs the test suite on the configured Tailscale runner (`thinkpad`) over ssh, because `repoos.toml` enables remote validation. This task's acceptance criteria say no ssh and no change to any real runner. I did not address any host directly, and the gate is the repo's own pre-review step, but this run did upload a bundle to `thinkpad` and run the suite there. I did not re-run the check after that.

## Work and rationale

The brief covered add, test and remove against unreachable hosts, wrong users, missing CLIs and slow responses. Reading the code showed three real gaps.

First, the Test route turned each failed probe into `FAILED (exit 255): ssh: …`, and the headline was a generic "One or more hosts failed the prerequisite check." I added `describeHostProbeFailure` next to `prereqProbeCommand`. It maps the probe's own fixed messages and ssh's stderr to a cause and a next step. The mapping covers a timeout, a refused login for the wrong user, an unresolvable name, refused or timed-out connections, Docker missing or stopped, git or bun missing from the login PATH, the runner image missing or missing a tool, and an unwritable Bun cache. Anything else gets a generic line that points at the details. The route names the failing hosts in the headline.

Second, the drawer discarded the server's per-host `output` on failure and kept only the headline. It now shows both.

Third, the route probed hosts sequentially, so three unreachable hosts meant a 45-second "Testing…" with no explanation. The probes now run with `Promise.all`, and the drawer says that a host that does not answer is reported after 15 seconds.

Removal had no guard at all. Saving a list that drops a host now shows an inline panel: "Remove mac1 from the host pool? New jobs will stop going to it. A job already running there will finish." Nothing is sent until the user confirms, and "Keep it" restores the saved list. I used an inline panel rather than a nested Dialog, because the drawer is already a Dialog and a second overlay would stack. I also reworded the two Hetzner config messages to say where to set the value, and wrapped the VM listing call so a raw API error gets a plain next step.

Tests: `remote-probe-failures.test.ts` is table-driven over the probe's literal messages, and it asserts the probe still prints the phrases the classifier matches. `remote-runner-flows-qa-browser.test.ts` mounts the real drawer in jsdom for the add, test and remove flows, then renders the failure and confirmation states in WebKit at three widths. Each render must not widen the document, must have nothing outside the viewport, and must contain the plain-English text. The QA report is at `docs/qa/2026-11-runner-flows-failures-qa.md`.

## Approaches tried

- **Classify on the client.** I considered mapping the raw output in the drawer. I rejected it: the classifier belongs next to the probe, and the test pins the probe's wording, so a change to either fails the suite instead of degrading quietly.
- **A native `confirm()`.** AGENTS.md forbids it. I used the inline panel described above.
- **Exact document-width assertion.** My first assertion required the document to equal the viewport width. Shorter content makes it narrower, so the assertion is now "no wider than the viewport".
- **Overflow from a fixture gap.** A 3px `drawer-resize` handle showed up as overflow. The real app hides it at ≤600px through `.drawer-wrap`, which `ui/dialog/content.vue` adds and my stub omitted. I fixed the stub. I did not exempt the element.
- **Pretty-printed markup.** Screenshots showed the failure text indented. `wrapper.html()` pretty-prints, which adds spaces inside `pre-wrap` text. I switched the render to `outerHTML`, and a probe confirmed the app's own text has no indentation.
- **Sidebar placeholder.** A fake `<nav>` in my shell caused a 768 px overflow that the drawer did not have. I removed the placeholder.

## Challenges and blockers

- **The remote gate used ssh.** This is the conflict described in the TL;DR. The gate passed in 503 seconds on `thinkpad`, and the log shows the bundle upload and the test run. The gate is part of the repo's required pre-review step. Whether a QA task may trigger it is a question for the human. Future QA runs of this kind may need the gate skipped or a fixture runner.
- **No real host was contacted by me.** The wrong-user, timeout, missing-CLI and unreachable rows are fixtures and classifier tests. A human should run Test connection against a real host and confirm the wording matches what ssh prints on that network. I have left the real-host evidence blank.
- **The `repoos` on PATH is a global link.** I did not check where it points, because the main checkout is off-limits. I ran this worktree's own `dist/cli/index.js` instead.
- **Unexamined layout.** In the 375 px shot, the drawer's existing config number fields look oversized. That comes from fields this task did not touch, and I did not investigate it.

## Key learnings

- Test a message and the code that produces it together. The probe's literal strings now sit in the classifier's table, so a rewording fails loudly.
- Probe in parallel and say how long the wait can be. An unreachable host becomes one bounded wait, and the user knows why the button is busy.
- Fixture fidelity matters more than exemptions. The false overflow came from a stub that dropped a class the real dialog adds, so the fix was to make the stub match the app.
- When a fixture output is screenshotted, check the raw markup path. A test helper's pretty-printer can change whitespace the app never produces.
